title: Central vs neutral extension: cumulative revenue excluding Australia

claims.text: The two scenario estimates are close, so switching the extension of the event beyond the official forecast horizon to a neutral decay path only modestly reduces the modeled cumulative aggregate mean revenue loss excluding Australia; this is a scenario comparison, not evidence of causal attribution, and the sensitivity alternatives do not define a calibrated credible interval or carry occurrence probabilities.

limitations: Scenario names are labels, not ratios to the fitted central parameters; actual fitted parameters were not read for this comparison.
Sensitivity alternatives are not assigned occurrence probabilities and do not bracket a calibrated credible interval.
The scenario difference reflects a modeling extension choice beyond the official forecast horizon, not a causal attribution.
The extension used beyond the official forecast horizon is not itself a NOAA forecast; official forecasts are marginal, not joint.
Historical input provenance is incomplete; the assessment is provided for inspection only and was not recomputed.
Estimates are conditional on the event pipeline's agriculture and fiscal-capture model scope; historical supporting assumptions do not transfer to other models.
Values are mean signed revenue losses (neutral revenue minus event revenue); gains are retained in signed estimates, and these means are not tail (VaR/ES) shortfall measures.
The aggregate excludes Australia and covers the modeled countries only; country-level quantiles were not summed or evaluated.
